answer: Require each identity to keep a public cedar logbook in which every attempt is written with a quill before its outcome is known, intermediate steps sealed so they cannot be edited later, then publish the failures as well as the successes. A genuine worker's dead ends are hard to invent after the fact; a sybil operator must either fabricate a distinct, plausible failure history for every shell in advance, work scaling with the shells and risking contradictions when the seals open, or reuse one history and expose the cluster by identical dead ends, each entry quartz-timed to its epoch.
